description.purpose: The container this member's assistants are instantiated into. It ships empty and open: no cells, no ports, no contract of its own. Its whole job is to be an address that already exists, so the mutation that instantiates an assistant has somewhere to put one -- and so the member can wire its holders to that address once instead of once per agent.
description.use_when: Never on its own -- it travels with member@1.1.0. Address it as <member>/assistants in the add_nodes of the mutation that instantiates an assistant, and draw that assistant's own edges in the same mutation. TRANSIT, derived from the contract of assistant@1.1.0 and from what this member sends back down (firewall@2.0.5, memory-hive@3.0.3) -- IN, the two a sibling of this container produces: in_turn (the screened turn coming back from ./firewall on pass) and in_bundle (the memory hive's answer). The four an assistant ALSO accepts -- in_advice, in_sweep, in_prune, in_round_sweep -- are deliberately NOT lanes of the member (ruling W7-R5): their producer is ./cogny inside the assistant, a second agent standing beside it in this container, or an operator or timer, and each of those addresses <member>/assistants/<agent> at its own path. That is allowed because neither this level nor the assistant declares params.ports, so both are open and the port boundary refuses an outside endpoint only for a SEALED hive. A lane a level declares but nothing ever crosses it on is the mirror image of one it emits with no edge -- see templates/member/README.md. OUT, the seven an assistant emits: turn, write, turn_write, extraction, recall, prune, error. Three of them stop at this level -- turn at ./firewall, recall and extraction at ./memory-hive -- and extraction is the one that must not stop HERE, in the container: it is the write half of the member's memory (GH #122, ADR 0012), wired the way talky's own recipe prescribes, two edges and never one. The other four -- write, turn_write, prune, error -- are re-emitted by the member on its own contract and leave the level; the parent drains them.
description.not_in_scope: No ports, because a sealed hive refuses exactly the endpoints an assistant instantiation needs (hive_port_boundary). No slot: GH #285's slot governs an address that does not exist, and this container does exist, so the declared unbound word could never fire -- see unbound_slot_behaviour in crates/meclaw-colony/src/colony.rs, which steps aside as soon as the target is a registered hive scope. No params.contract either: this container is wired by the member the moment the member is instantiated, and a contracted hive whose declared lanes have no door or exit INSIDE it refuses every later mutation in the colony (mutation::hive_contract::check_lane_doors, via hive_path_is_wired). The transit list above is therefore prose the instantiating mutation reads, not a declaration the substrate would enforce against an empty container. No cells: what stands in this container is an assistant, and an assistant is instantiated, never shipped.
